goal: The nightly measures a repository only when there is something new to measure. A tick that finds the remote default branch sitting at the commit the last measurement already covered runs no suite for that repository, records that it measured nothing, and says why. A repository whose branch has moved is measured exactly as it is today.

The cadence itself does not change: one tick every 24 h counted from the last finished tick, `DEFAULT_INTERVAL_MS` in `src/mc/nightly.js`. What changes is what a tick costs on a day when nothing landed.
contract: A skip on an unchanged tree is recorded as a run that measured nothing, never as a pass. `storedRun` in `src/mc/nightly-history.js` decides that by the *type* of `red`: an array means the suite reached its own summary, `null` means it did not. An unchanged skip passes `red: null`, so `outcome` is `incomplete` and the run is transparent to the red-streak walk in `standing()` — it neither continues a streak nor breaks one. A skip that arrived as `red: []` would read as a green night and is the exact false green this whole meter exists to remove.

Fail open. Any failure to learn the remote head — no network, no `origin`, a git error, an empty answer — runs the round. The ticks of 2026-09-08T17:21Z and 2026-09-09T17:42Z in `~/.memoro/mc/nightly/nightly.log` both stopped at fetch with `fatal: unable to access 'https://github.com/martinforsberg81/memoro.git/': Could not resolve host: github.com`, and each was written down as a stopped round naming that reason. That outcome must stay reachable. An offline machine must never produce a silent skip that looks like a quiet night.
The tick still visits every repository `knownRepos()` lists, in the order it lists them. The condition removes work for a repository, never a repository from the list.

The nightly stays a meter. It commits nothing, pushes nothing, writes nothing inside a repository, takes no branch, and blocks no merge round. The lock guard at the top of each repository's turn in `nightlyTick` is unchanged: a live gate round still ends the tick rather than queueing behind it.

The existing seams in `nightlyTick` stay injectable. `tests/mc/nightly.test.js` drives it with `repos`, `round` and `clock` and touches no git and no network; whatever learns the remote head joins them as a parameter with a real default, not a bare call into `git`.
out_of_scope: What drives the tick. This project changes the body of `nightlyTick`; who calls it is `nightly-is-a-chore`, which follows this one in the queue and moves the whole thing into the runner's `chores()` so that `mc run stop` stops it. Write the skip so it does not care which of the two is driving: a parameter with a default, not a reach into process state.

Starting the nightly by itself, at login or on a timer or by any other means. Ruling 9 of 2026-09-04 says nothing on this machine runs by itself, with the nightly named, and ruling 23 of 2026-09-19 goes further and takes its process away. This project does not touch either.

Making the nightly's own liveness visible anywhere it is not visible today. Martin ruled on 2026-09-19 that the nightly's death is not to appear in the brief (ruling 23). Nothing here changes what the brief or `mc deploy` read.
Any change to what `full` selects or runs, to `deferredRules` in memoro's `config/testing-registry.mjs`, or to the gate.

A second cadence, a catch-up burst, a queue for missed nights, or any notion of a run being overdue. A tick that skips is followed by the next tick one interval later, exactly as a tick that measured is.

success_criteria.criterion: A repository whose remote default branch is at the commit of its last measurement is not measured, and the skip is written down as a run that measured nothing.
success_criteria.check: In `tests/mc/nightly.test.js`, a tick whose injected head probe returns the same sha the stored history carries: the injected `round` is never called, and `readNightlyHistory` gains one entry whose `red` is `null` and whose `outcome` is `incomplete`.

success_criteria.criterion: A repository whose remote default branch has moved is measured exactly as before.
success_criteria.check: Same test file: the probe returns a different sha, `round` is called once for that repository, and the stored run carries the commit and the red names the report gave.

success_criteria.criterion: A head that cannot be read is measured, not skipped.
success_criteria.check: Same test file, two cases: a probe that returns `null` and a probe that throws. Both call `round` once. Neither writes a skip.

success_criteria.criterion: A repository that has never been measured is measured.
success_criteria.check: Same test file: an empty history with any head value calls `round` once. There is no commit to compare against, so there is no case in which the first tick on a fresh machine is skipped.

success_criteria.criterion: Red-since is unchanged by a skip that sat between two measurements.
success_criteria.check: In `tests/mc/nightly-history.test.js`, a history of measured-red, then an unchanged skip, then measured-red with the same name: `nightlyReading().red[0].since` is the timestamp of the first red run, and `runs` counts two, not one.

success_criteria.criterion: `mc test nightly status` says the repository was skipped because nothing changed, and still shows the last real measurement and its commit.
success_criteria.check: Run `mc test nightly status` against a home whose history ends in an unchanged skip. The repository's block names the skip and its reason, and the `full run` line still reports the earlier measurement's verdict, count and sha — the two lines `nightlyReading` already separates as `last` and `measured`.

documents.label: Why the nightly carries work no pull-request round runs — the deferred tests and the retired blanket

steps.title: A tick skips a repository whose branch has not moved since the last measurement
steps.done_when: `nightlyTick` asks each repository for its remote default-branch head before measuring it, skips the repository when that head equals the commit of the last run in its history that actually measured something, and records the skip as a run with `red: null`; every other outcome, including every failure to learn the head, measures as before.
instruction: The work is in `src/mc/nightly-loop.js`, in `nightlyTick`. Read the whole file first, including its header — the loop's shape and the reasons for it are written there and this change has to fit them rather than sit beside them.

Today the per-repository body of `nightlyTick` does three things in order: it asks `runningRound({ root })` whether a gate round holds the lock and ends the tick if so, it calls `round({ repoPath, root, env, say })`, and it turns the report into a `run` object which it pushes onto `runs`, hands to `recordNightlyRun` and prints through `line()`. Add one thing between the lock guard and the call to `round`: learn this repository's remote head, compare it to what was last measured, and when they are equal write a skip and `continue` to the next repository. Note the difference from the existing `skipped` path — that one `break`s, because a busy lock is a fact about the machine and the rest of the tick would hit the same lock. An unchanged repository is a fact about that repository alone, so the tick goes on to the next one.

Learning the head. `git ls-remote origin HEAD` prints the sha of the remote's default branch followed by a tab and `HEAD`, and it is one network round-trip with no fetch and nothing written to the repository. That is the right probe here: the tick must not fetch, because fetching is the round's own first act (`src/mc/repo-gate.js` line 330 runs `git fetch origin --prune` and line 343 records `report.base.commit` as `rev-parse` of the base ref) and a second fetch in the scheduler would be a second place that can fail differently. Use `tryGit` from `src/mc/git.js`, which returns `null` rather than throwing on a non-zero exit. Wrap the call so that a throw is caught too — `tryGit` swallows git's exit status but not, for instance, a spawn failure — and treat `null`, an empty string, anything that does not parse to a 40-character hex sha, and any thrown error identically: the head is unknown, and an unknown head measures.

Make the probe a parameter of `nightlyTick` alongside `repos`, `round` and `clock` — for instance `head = remoteHead` — with the real implementation as its default, so `tests/mc/nightly.test.js` can drive every branch of this without git and without a network. The existing tests in that file construct repositories as `{ name, path }` objects with paths like `/repos/memoro` that do not exist on disk; a probe that shelled out unconditionally would break them.

What to compare against. The last commit that was actually measured is not simply the last entry in the history: a history can end in a skip, or in a round that stopped at fetch, and both of those carry `commit: null` or a commit nothing was measured on. `nightlyReading(repoPath, { root })` in `src/mc/nightly-history.js` already draws exactly this distinction and returns `measured`, the last run whose `red` was an array, separately from `last`, the last attempt of any kind. Use `nightlyReading(...).measured?.commit`. When it is absent — a repository never measured, or a history of nothing but stopped rounds — there is nothing to compare and the repository is measured.

Skip only on an exact string match between the probe's sha and that commit. Do not try to decide whether the branch moved forward or backward, and do not ask git about ancestry: the probe deliberately does not fetch, so this checkout may not hold the remote commit at all, and an ancestry question would be answered wrongly or not at all. Equal means measured; anything else, including a shorter or differently-cased string, means measure.

What the skip records. Build the same kind of object the measured path builds and hand it to `recordNightlyRun({ ... }, { root })`, with `repo`, `path`, `started_at` as the tick's own clock reading, `duration_ms` as the little the probe cost, `commit` set to the head that was found, `verdict` `stopped`, a new `stopped_at` value of `unchanged`, a `reason` naming the sha and where it was last measured, and `red: null`. The `red: null` is the load-bearing part and the contract turns on it: `storedRun` reads the type of that field to decide between `incomplete` and a pass, and `standing()` walks only the runs whose `red` is an array, so an `incomplete` entry leaves every red streak dated exactly where it was. Push the object onto `runs` as well, so the tick's return value describes what it did.

Say one line for it, in the register the other lines use — `line()` at the bottom of the file formats a run as `<repo>  <what>  started <at>  took <s>  main <sha7> — <tail>`, and a skip should read as a sentence a person scanning the log understands without pairing it with anything: the repository, that it was unchanged, the sha, and when that sha was last measured. Follow `line()`'s shape rather than inventing a second one; extending `line()` to handle `stopped_at === 'unchanged'` is better than a separate writer.

Then make `mc test nightly status` say it. That page is `status()` in `src/mc/commands/test.js` around line 552, which builds one block per repository from `nightlyState()` and `nightlyReading(repo.path)` and renders through `renderNightlyLines` in `src/mc/repo-render.js`. It already prints two separate facts where they differ — the last attempt and the last measurement — which is precisely the pair this change creates more of: after a quiet week the last attempt is `unchanged` and the last measurement is a week old and still true of the commit it names. Read `renderNightlyLines` and make the `unchanged` attempt render as what it is. It must not read as a failure, because nothing failed, and it must not hide the measurement it did not replace.

Tests. Extend `tests/mc/nightly.test.js` with the four tick cases the criteria name — equal head, different head, unreadable head (both `null` and a throw), and empty history — each asserting on whether the injected `round` was called and on what `readNightlyHistory` holds afterwards. Extend `tests/mc/nightly-history.test.js` with the streak case: measured-red, unchanged skip, measured-red, and assert `nightlyReading().red[0].since` is the first of the two and that the skip did not restart the streak. Run `npm test` in the repository root when you are done and put its result in the pull request.

One thing to be careful about that the code does not show. The commit stored by a measured run is `report.base?.commit || report.candidate?.commit`, which for a `--full` round is `rev-parse origin/<default>` taken after that round's own fetch. `git ls-remote origin HEAD` resolves the remote's default branch through `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD`'s upstream equivalent, so on these two repositories the two answers are the same string for the same tree. If you find a repository where they are not — a checkout whose `origin/HEAD` points somewhere other than the branch the round measures — do not paper over it by comparing prefixes or by fetching. Stop and say so in the pull request: a probe that names a different branch than the round measures would skip on the wrong evidence, which is worse than not skipping at all.
